newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rand/dlr weakness masks wider forex strength-Stals.
newsitem.headline: Rand/dlr weakness masks wider forex strength-Stals.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals on Thursday signalled he was not alarmed by the rand's decline to a six-month low against the dollar, saying this reflected U.S. dollar strength rather than rand weakness.
Stals told Reuters there had been no change in the central bank's exchange rate policy which remained to "lean against the wind" and provide liquidity as necessary.

The rand earlier fell to 4.6140 bid against the dollar from from 4.5910 overnight, but Stals warned not to overlook its performance against mark, yen and sterling -- all as important for South African trade as the dollar.
"The rand has not depreciated against the basket in the last few days -- as a matter of fact the rand has been very strong against the basket," he said.
The currency had appreciated by around 4.5 percent on a trade-weighted basis since the start of the year, he added.

Currency dealers have reported that the Reserve bank has adopted a lower profile in the foreign exchange markets in the last couple of weeks compared with the prominent intervention which marked the beginning of the month.
But Stals dismissed suggestions that this signalled he was no longer interested in defending the rand.
"We were much more active in the market in the first two weeks but that was during the period of the introduction of the new exchange controls and the decline in the gold price," he said.
"But that does not mean that in the last two weeks we have taken a different view on the exchange rate."

South Africa relaxed exchange controls on individuals from July 1, allowing them to invest up to 200,000 rand offshore for the first time, while at the same time bullion sank to a 12-year low of $314 an ounce, squeezing the mining sector.
